text096: Mr. Lian Haomin has extensive corporate governance experience through investing in and managing numerous companies. He founded Da Sheng Group Holdings Limited, a fintech group focused on one-stop financial services, with subsidiaries licensed by the Hong Kong SFC for Type 1, Type 4 and Type 9 regulated activities. He also chairs Ever Rich International Limited, which invests primarily in overseas real estate. His public and community roles include membership of the sixth Hong Kong Election Committee and the 13th All-China Youth Federation; chief president of the ninth Kowloon Federation of Associations; membership of the 64th Personal Data (Privacy) Advisory Committee; director of the Tung Wah Group of Hospitals for 2021/2022; vice-chairman of the fourth executive committee of the Hong Kong CPPCC Youth Association; executive committee member and deputy secretary-general of the 14th executive committee of the Hong Kong Elites Association; Hong Kong and Macao committee member of the 11th Jiangsu Youth Federation; standing director of the 29th Hong Kong Youth Federation; honorary director of the eighth Southern Youth Association; vice-chairman and secretary-general of the Youth Encouragement Fund; and honorary director of the University of Hong Kong Foundation.
text099: Mr. Zheng Yaowu has extensive experience in Hong Kong law enforcement and international anti-money laundering work, contributing to compliance across the Group's engineering and fintech businesses. Since April 2019, he has served as an executive director of a consultancy specializing in anti-money laundering and financial crime investigations. He retired from the Hong Kong Police Force in September 2018 as an assistant commissioner. From 2007 to 2010, he headed the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit and led the financial investigation team, overseeing major money laundering cases and delivering training to local and international law enforcement, regulators, financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses and professions. In 2006 and 2007, he was seconded to the Security Bureau to coordinate anti-money laundering legislation and operations, and helped prepare Hong Kong's 2008 FATF assessment. He served on the World Economic Forum's organized crime council from 2012 to 2015, and on the Wildlife Justice Commission from 2015 to 2023, including its supervisory board from 2022 to 2023. He holds a Bachelor of Science (1986) and a Master of Public Administration (2004) from the University of Hong Kong.

quotaHoldBody1: The position limit is set from the proof of assets and risk assessment you submitted during KYC. It caps the virtual assets you may hold. The remaining limit is what you can still buy with fiat; once the value you hold exceeds the limit you may no longer buy with fiat, but you can still sell.
quotaHoldBody2: Only fiat pair purchases count against the position limit. Crypto-to-crypto trades (e.g. BTC/USDC) are unrestricted, and the daily recovery never exceeds the daily trading limit.
quotaHoldBody3: Credited deposits count as used position, while completed withdrawals restore the used limit.
quotaHoldBody4: When nothing remains, or to request a larger limit, contact us with additional proof of assets.
quotaDailyBody1: The daily trading limit (UTC+8, 00:00-23:59:59) is the value you can buy with fiat each day. It resets at 00:00 and equals half of the holding limit.

proInvestorP1: Under the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Ordinance, professional investors include institutional, corporate and individual professional investors.
proInvestorP2: Institutional professional investors are the persons defined in Schedule 1, Part 1, section 1 of the Ordinance, such as recognised exchanges, clearing houses, intermediaries, authorised financial institutions, authorised insurers, recognised collective investment schemes, registered MPF schemes, occupational retirement schemes and governments.
proInvestorP3: Corporate professional investors are the trusts, corporations and partnerships under sections 4, 6 and 7 of the Securities and Futures (Professional Investor) Rules: a trust corporation needs total assets of at least HKD 40 million (or its equivalent), while a corporation or partnership needs a portfolio of at least HKD 8 million or total assets of at least HKD 40 million.
proInvestorP4: An individual professional investor is a person under section 5 of the Rules with a portfolio of at least HKD 8 million (or its equivalent), such as cash, deposits and securities defined by the Ordinance.
